detected_issues.entity: FHIR ontology reuse as encoded in FASTO
detected_issues.evidence: Primary RDF/XML parsed as https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO.owl with owl:versionIRI https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/FASTO.owl/1.0 and no owl:imports triples detected. Paper states that FASTO uses FHIR STU3; most treatment-plan features are imported from a FHIR model; FHIR resources are profiled, fields are added/removed, constraints changed, and extensions/customizations of selected resources are implemented for T1D.
detected_issues.explanation: FASTO reuses and customizes FHIR terms, but the authoritative RDF/XML contains no owl:imports statement tying the model to the supplied FHIR ontology or to a specific FHIR ontology artifact.
detected_issues.suggested_fix: Add an explicit owl:imports or documented extraction/profiling module for the selected FHIR version, or place FASTO-specific FHIR profiles in FASTO-owned IRIs with mappings to FHIR.

detected_issues.entity: all exact-match FHIR classes and object properties in directly_reused_entities
detected_issues.evidence: Primary RDF/XML contains additional subject triples for every exact FHIR class and object property relative to the supplied FHIR TTL; examples include rdfs:subClassOf, rdfs:domain, rdfs:range, and rdfs:subPropertyOf axioms listed in directly_reused_entities.axioms.
detected_issues.explanation: FHIR entities are reused under their original IRIs while receiving FASTO-specific subclass, domain, range, subproperty, and datatype restriction axioms. This can alter interpretation of reused FHIR terms outside a local profiling context.
detected_issues.suggested_fix: Represent constraints in a FASTO profile namespace or SHACL/OWL profile module and connect them to FHIR entities using explicit mapping or profile annotations.

detected_issues.entity: non-exact declarations in http://hl7.org/fhir/ listed in local_entities_in_reused_namespace
detected_issues.evidence: Primary RDF/XML declares FHIR-namespace classes/properties that are absent from the supplied FHIR ontology; paper states FHIR profiling, added/removed fields, changed constraints, and selected-resource customizations.
detected_issues.explanation: FASTO appears to create or profile domain-specific entities inside the HL7 FHIR namespace instead of a FASTO namespace. Some may be intended FHIR profiles, but the RDF/XML does not distinguish profiles from source FHIR entities.
detected_issues.suggested_fix: Mint FASTO-owned IRIs for profiles/extensions and map them to FHIR resource/property IRIs with rdfs:subClassOf, owl:equivalentClass, or explicit profile annotations where appropriate.

detected_issues.entity: all declarations in https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/fhir.owl# listed in local_entities_in_reused_namespace
detected_issues.evidence: Primary RDF/XML uses https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/fhir.owl# for sensor platforms, measurement capabilities, properties, and individuals; the supplied FHIR TTL uses http://hl7.org/fhir/ and has no named individuals.
detected_issues.explanation: The BioPortal fhir.owl namespace is separate from the supplied FHIR namespace and is used for entities that appear to be FASTO-specific sensor or patient-monitoring content.
detected_issues.suggested_fix: Move these entities to the FASTO namespace and link them to FHIR or SSN terms with explicit mappings.

detected_issues.evidence: Paper states FASTO depends on FHIR STU3; primary RDF/XML has ontology versionInfo 1.0 but no FHIR owl:imports or FHIR version IRI.
detected_issues.explanation: Maintainers cannot determine from the RDF/XML alone which FHIR ontology release is the normative dependency.
detected_issues.suggested_fix: Record the FHIR release/version IRI and exact source artifact used to generate or profile the included terms.

summary.main_problem: FHIR is reused and profiled without an explicit import or clean separation between source FHIR IRIs and FASTO-specific profile/extension IRIs.
summary.maintenance_risk: FHIR release changes or profile evolution can silently affect hundreds of reused properties and locally minted FHIR-namespace entities.
summary.recommended_action: Use explicit FHIR version provenance and move FASTO-specific profiles/extensions into FASTO-owned namespaces with mappings to FHIR.
